_comment: The REWORK Proof MCP server's tools and the fixed sentences it returns, in one file. Two servers read it: this package (stdio, index.js beside this file) and the hosted server REWORK runs at https://api.reworkdigital.io/mcp, so neither can describe a tool, or the ceiling on a claim, differently from the other. Every tool only reads: readOnlyHint is true on all of them.

server.name: rework-proof
server.title: REWORK Proof
server.description: Check whether delivered work is genuinely the author's: verify a REWORK credential or certificate, see whether it was revoked or ever issued, and read what it does and does not prove.
server.instructions: Read `assurance_note` with every result: it states the ceiling on what the result proves. A valid signature is not a review of the work.

protocols._comment: Revisions of the Model Context Protocol this server speaks, newest first. `handshake` revisions begin with `initialize`. `stateless` revisions have no handshake: every request names its revision in `params._meta`.

tools.name: verify_rework_credential
tools.title: Verify a REWORK credential
tools.description: Check whether a REWORK Verifiable Credential (a VC-JWT) is authentic, and report what it claims. Use this when someone presents a credential as evidence that they produced a piece of work. Returns whether the signature is valid, whether REWORK has since revoked it, who issued it, and the credential subject.

credential.description: The compact VC-JWT, three base64url segments separated by dots.

valid.description: True only when the signature verifies against REWORK's key, the credential has not expired, and REWORK has not revoked it.

reason.description: Why the credential is not valid; null when it is.

revoked.description: True when REWORK revoked the credential after issuing it; false when it was checked and stands; null when there is nothing to check (not a certificate credential, or not valid) or the status could not be read.

issuer.description: Who issued the credential, as the credential states it; null when it is not valid.

credential_subject.description: What the credential claims. Empty when it is not valid.

assurance_note.description: The ceiling on what this result proves. Read it before relying on the result.

credential_type.description: Which kind of REWORK credential this is, as the credential states it; null when it is not valid or not a known kind.

tools.name: get_rework_issuer_keys
tools.title: Get REWORK's public signing keys
tools.description: Fetch REWORK's public signing keys (JWKS). Use this to verify a credential offline yourself instead of trusting this server, or to confirm the issuer key a credential names actually belongs to REWORK.

keys.description: REWORK's public signing keys, as a JSON Web Key Set.

tools.name: explain_rework_assurance
tools.title: Explain a REWORK assurance level
tools.description: Explain what a REWORK assurance level or credential type proves, and what it explicitly does not prove. Use this before relying on a credential, so a weak claim is not read as a strong one.

assurance.description: Assurance level, e.g. "workflow-identity". Omit to list all.

outputSchema.description: One level when `assurance` was given, every level otherwise, or `error` with the known levels when the level asked for does not exist.

tools.name: lookup_rework_attestation
tools.title: Look up whether REWORK issued a credential
tools.description: Check whether REWORK actually ISSUED a credential - not just whether its signature verifies. A forged-but-well-formed token fails this; a real one returns its issuance record and the CURRENT OpenTimestamps receipt, which may have been upgraded to a Bitcoin confirmation since issue. Pass the credential (its sha256 is the lookup key) or the digest directly. Workflow attestations and Hugging Face credentials are recorded. Certificate, video-receipt and passport credentials are signed afresh on every download and have no issuance record: pass the credential itself (not its digest) and the answer says so, with the certificate it names looked up instead.

credential.description: The VC-JWT. Only its sha256 digest is used as the lookup key; the credential itself is not stored. For a certificate credential, the certificate id it names is looked up as well.

digest.description: sha256 hex of the credential, if you already have it.

issued.description: Whether REWORK has a record of issuing a credential with this digest. Null when REWORK keeps no per-digest record for this kind of credential, so the lookup can neither confirm nor deny it.

assurance_note.description: The ceiling on what this result proves. Read it before relying on the result.

credential_type.description: The kind of credential: from REWORK's record when one was found, otherwise as the credential states it (unverified).

certificate.description: Present for a certificate credential: the certificate it names, looked up by id.

found.description: Whether REWORK has that certificate; null when it could not be read.

revoked.description: Whether it has been revoked; null when not found or not read.

github.description: For a Hugging Face join: the GitHub Actions run, as REWORK recorded it.

huggingface.description: For a Hugging Face credential: the repository (and for a join, the exact content state) REWORK recorded.

claim.description: For a repository-control challenge: the claim's state now (status, verdict, lease). Only a status of verified shows control today.

timestamp.description: The OpenTimestamps receipt as REWORK holds it now. Only a status of confirmed is anchored in Bitcoin.

annotations.title: Look up whether REWORK issued a credential

tools.name: check_rework_certificate
tools.title: Check a REWORK certificate by ID or link
tools.description: Check a REWORK certificate from its ID or its link, which is what people usually share: whether REWORK holds it, whether it is active or revoked, and what its public page shows (holder, title, issue date, verified proofs and skills, and a verified result when there is one). Use this when you are given a certificate ID (such as RW-CERT-...) or a link to /verify/... or /certificates/share/....

annotations.title: Check a REWORK certificate by ID or link

certificate.description: A certificate ID, or a link to a REWORK certificate page (/verify/<id> or /certificates/share/<token>).

found.description: Whether REWORK holds a certificate under this ID or link. Null when the records could not be read just now.

active.description: Whether the certificate is active. Null when unknown.

revoked.description: Whether REWORK revoked it. Null when unknown.

status.description: The certificate's status as REWORK records it.

certificate.description: What the public page shows, for an active certificate only: holder, title, issued_at, verified_proofs, verified_skills, and verified_result when there is one.

assurance_note.description: The ceiling on what this result proves. Read it before relying on the result.

credential_types.REWORKWorkflowAttestation: A CI run whose repository identity GitHub attested via OIDC.
credential_types.REWORKHfJoinedPublication: A Hugging Face publication joined to the CI run that preceded it, confirmed by REWORK's own read of the Hub.
credential_types.REWORKHfRepoControl: A challenge REWORK issued to prove write control of a Hugging Face repository. It shows control only while REWORK holds the claim as verified.
credential_types.REWORKProofOfWorkCredential: A submitted piece of work that passed REWORK verification.
credential_types.REWORKVideoProvenanceReceipt: A reviewed demonstration video, fingerprinted against reuse.
credential_types.REWORKReputationPassport: A holder's full verified history in one signed credential.
credential_types.REWORKReputationSummary: A summary of already-public verified facts about a holder.

ai_declaration.reads: Commit messages only: a Co-authored-by, Assisted-by or Generated-by trailer naming one of the tools below; an Assisted-by trailer in the AGENT:MODEL form; a Claude-Session, Amp-Thread-ID or Replit-Commit-Author trailer; an `AI-assisted: true` line; or a "Generated with" line.
ai_declaration.zero_means: No commit message declared a tool. It does not mean no tool was used; a message with no trailer looks the same either way.
ai_declaration.declared_means: The author chose to say so. It is reported as a fact and never lowers a result.

notes.unknown_assurance: Assurance level not recognised - do not assume this proves more than it states.
notes.issued: Issuance confirms REWORK signed a credential with this digest. It is still not a review of the code or a claim the work is any good - and a "submitted" timestamp is a calendar promise, only "confirmed" means anchored in Bitcoin.
notes.not_issued: REWORK has no record of issuing a credential with this digest. A valid signature with no issuance record deserves suspicion: it could predate the registry, or it could be a key compromise.
notes.revoked: REWORK revoked this credential after issuing it. Its signature still verifies, which is exactly why revocation has to be checked: do not rely on it.
notes.revocation_unchecked: Whether this credential has since been revoked could not be checked just now. The signature is valid; treat the result as incomplete.
notes.no_assurance_level: This type of credential carries no assurance level. A valid signature shows REWORK issued it and that it has not been altered; it is not a review of how good the work is.
notes.registry_not_kept: REWORK keeps no per-digest record for this type of credential: it is signed afresh each time it is downloaded, so no two copies share a digest, and this lookup can neither confirm nor deny it. That is not a sign of forgery. Check its signature with verify_rework_credential; what the credential says about itself here is unverified until then.
notes.registry_newest_only: REWORK keeps a record of only the newest repository-control challenge for each person and repository: starting the ceremony again replaces it. An older challenge missing here is not a sign of forgery. Check its signature and expiry with verify_rework_credential; what the credential says about itself here is unverified until then.
notes.claim_not_current: REWORK issued this challenge, but the claim it belongs to is now {status}: it does not show control of the repository today.
notes.certificate_active: This is REWORK's current record of the certificate, as its public page shows it: a reviewer verified the work it lists. It is not a review of how good the work is, and a certificate can be revoked later, so check again before relying on it.
notes.certificate_revoked: REWORK revoked this certificate. Do not rely on it, or on any credential issued for it.
notes.certificate_inactive: REWORK holds this certificate, but it is not active, so its public page does not show it. Do not rely on it as it stands.
notes.certificate_not_found: REWORK holds no certificate under that ID or link. Check it was copied in full: this lookup cannot tell a mistyped ID from one that never existed.
notes.certificate_unreadable: REWORK's records could not be read just now, so nothing is known about this certificate either way. Try again shortly.

errors.credential_required: credential is required: pass the compact VC-JWT (three base64url segments separated by dots)
errors.digest_required: pass either `credential` (the VC-JWT) or `digest` (64 hex chars)
errors.certificate_required: certificate is required: pass a certificate ID (such as RW-CERT-...) or a link to a REWORK certificate page
errors.certificate_unrecognised: That is not a certificate ID or a REWORK certificate link. Pass the ID printed on the certificate, or its link (/verify/<id> or /certificates/share/<token>).
